sentences.text: Shri Shailendra Verma - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri G.S. Thakur - Ga for the State.
 Order

This is first bail application filed by the applicants under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No. 178/2024 dated 27.5.2024 registered at Police Station Gwarighat,
District Jabalpur for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 409, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The Collector, Jabalpur vide communication dated 24.5.2024 issued directions to the various Government Authorities to lodge the First Information Reports against the Management of various schools, Book Sellers, who were selling books to the students of the schools, publishers of the books as well as other employees like Principal of the School.
The Collector also uploaded a post on Facebook inviting parents of the students, if they had any complaints against the School Management.
It was also informed through the said post that the parents can verify International Standard Book Number (for short ISBN) from the website 2 MCRC-33117-2024 https://isbn.gov.in.
In response to the aforesaid, various complaints were received.

Thereafter, committees were constituted, which conducted enquiry and submitted their enquiry reports and on the basis of the said enquiry reports, the First Information Reports were lodged in few cases against the Principals of various Schools and in some cases against the Management and office bearer of the Managing Committee of the Schools, book sellers and publishers.
As per the case of the prosecution, the present applicants being book sellers prima facie are connected with the offence.
3. The counsel for the applicants contends that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the case.

It is contended that applicant No. 2 is aged about 70 years and suffering from multiple diseases, even in terms of the order passed by this Court dated 5.8.2024 in M.Cr.C. No.

1 30127 of 2024, a fresh medical report has been submitted, which clearly reflects that even at present applicant No. 2 is in Cardiology ICU.

sentences.text:
It is contended by the counsel looking to the age as well as ailment of the applicant, benefit of bail be granted to him as he is not in a position to suffer incarceration.
4.
It is further contended that applicant No. 1 is son-in-law of applicant No. 2 and is a Dentist by profession.
He has nothing to do with the business, which is being run by applicant No. 2.
Merely because on the unfateful day, he was sitting in the book shop owned by applicant No. 2, he has been implicated in the case.

It is further contended that no single document is available on record to demonstrate that applicant No. 1 has any connection with M/s Children Book House, licence of which is in the name of applicant 3 MCRC-33117-2024 No. 2.
Therefore, applicant No. 1 also deserves to be released on bail.
5. Per contra, the counsel for the State submits that the application filed by the applicants is liable to be dismissed.

Applicant No. 2 was making complaint since last 6 days regarding shortness of breathe and chest discomfort and due treatment is being given and, therefore, it cannot be said that incarceration is going to affect the health of applicant No. 2.

So far as applicant No. 1 is concerned,
his statement is there and seizure of entire documents like licence of M/s Children Book House,
GSTR Certificate, IT return and audit report were seized from applicant No. 1.

It is, therefore,
contended that no case for grant of bail is made out to applicant No. 1 also.

6. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
7.
On perusal of the material available on record, it reflects that the FIR was lodged on 27.5.2024 and the investigation in the matter is still going on.
A report regarding health condition of applicant No. 2 has been submitted by the State in M.Cr.C. No. 30127 of 2024.

A perusal of report reflects that applicant No. 2 is suffering from K/C/O DM2 Uncontrolled Blood Sugar with HTN with CVA Rt.
Hemiparesis (Left Parietal Bleed) 2007 with Ocular Myasthenica (2021).
Now with Dyspnea and Chest Discomfort under Evaluation with URTI and shortness of breath since 6 days, sweating since 6 days.

8. A perusal of report dated 8.8.2024 further reflects that applicant No. 2 has been shifted to Cardiology ICU for intensive care and further management.
9.
So far as applicant No. 1 is concerned, the State has not produced 4 MCRC-33117-2024 any document to indicate as to whether applicant No. 1 is the proprietor/owner of M/s Children Book House.

Applicant No. 1 is the son-in- law of applicant No. 2 and seizure has been made from applicant No. 1, who according to prosecution, himself has provided all the documents to the Authorities as his father-in-law/applicant No. 2 was indisposed.
It has been apprised to this Court during course of hearing that after seizure of the books, all the books have been released to applicant No. 2 on supurdginama.

10. Thus, looking to the age and illness of applicant No. 2 and nature of allegations against applicant No. 1, who prima facie, is not being shown to be owner/proprietor of M/s Children Book House, this Shashank Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23614671/

sentences.text: Court deems it to be a fit case to release both the applicants on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

11. It is directed that applicants namely Shashank Shrivastava and Surya Prakash Verma shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only)
each with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for their appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

12. It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE PB 5 MCRC-33117-2024 Shashank Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23614671/
